Gradient-topology toy dataset

Source: R/levi_datasets.R
gradient_dataset.Rd

A 6-node linear chain where expression increases monotonically from left (GA) to right (GF). Designed to verify that landscape scores preserve strict rank order along a gradient and that no spurious peaks appear in intermediate positions.

Format

Two tab-delimited files in inst/extdata/:

gradient_network.dat

Linear chain GA-GB-GC-GD-GE-GF with nodes equally spaced from x = 0.10 to x = 0.90 at y = 0.50.

gradient_expression.dat

Columns ID, Test, Control. Values increase from GA (Test = 5, Control = 100) to GF (Test = 100, Control = 5), giving a smooth gradient of signal ratios from ~ 0.09 to ~ 0.91.

Source

Simulated data generated for unit testing.

Value

NULL (this object documents data files, not a function)

Expected results

  • Strictly monotone scores: GA < GB < GC < GD < GE < GF.

  • GF ranked 1st; GA ranked last.

  • score(GF) > 0.5; score(GA) < 0.5.

  • No peak detected at intermediate nodes.

See also

levi, hub dataset

Examples

# \donttest{
grad_net  <- file.path(system.file(package = "levi"),
                        "extdata", "gradient_network.dat")
grad_expr <- file.path(system.file(package = "levi"),
                        "extdata", "gradient_expression.dat")

res <- levi(
    networkCoordinatesInput = grad_net,
    expressionInput         = grad_expr,
    fileTypeInput           = "dat",
    geneSymbolInput         = "ID",
    readExpColumn           = readExpColumn("Test-Control"),
    contrastValueInput      = 50,
    resolutionValueInput    = 50,
    zoomValueInput          = 50,
    smoothValueInput        = 50
)

res$scores[order(res$scores$Rank), c("Gene", "LandscapeScore", "Rank")]
#>   Gene LandscapeScore Rank
#> 1   GF         0.9370    1
#> 2   GE         0.7948    2
#> 3   GD         0.5438    3
#> 4   GC         0.4562    4
#> 5   GB         0.2052    5
#> 6   GA         0.0630    6
# }
